text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

English pioneer pharmacist CALEB SOUL was born on this day in 1817. He set-up business in Pitt Street in Sydney as WASHINGTON H. SOUL, named after his son, and his pharmacy featured a tr*ndy American soda fountain in 1888.
Irish journalist EDMUND FINN, who wrote the "Chronicles of Early Melbourne", was born in 1819.
Pioneer South Australian wine-grower THOMAS HARDY was born in 1830.
Australian steel engineer ESSINGTON LEWIS was born on this day in 1881. He introduced the "shadow-board" (outlines of tools drawn on a board), for the storage of tools.
Russian singer and vaudeville star SOPHIE TUCKER was born as SONIA KALISH in 1884.
Australian Rules Football legend ROY CAZALEY was born in 1893. His South Melbourne team-mate "SKEETER" FLEITER would call "Up There CAZALEY", and it became a national catchphrase.

Former Queensland Premier Sir JOH (Johannes) BJELKE-PETERSEN was born in New Zealand on this day in 1911. For almost 20 years, the former premier, was an icon of the National Party. Despite his long association with the party he did not attend the party's 75th anniversary celebrations in Melbourne on 11th January, 1995. He said "the members of today are not of the same calibre as some of the great people we've had down the years". Sir JOH stayed at home in Kingaroy and got ready for his own celebrations for his 84th birthday.
American actor ROBERT STACK was born in 1919.
The creator of the much-loved children's character "Paddington Bear", MICHAEL BOND, was born in 1926.

South African born musician TREVOR RABBIT was born in 1955. He played the guitar, bass and the keyboard as well as singing. He was with 'Rabbitt', 'Streetband', 'Manfred Mann's Earth Band', 'Yes' and performed with solo LP's such as "Wolf".

Brtish singer/songwriter GRAHAM McPHERSON was born in 1961. With the band 'Madness' in 1979 he had his first major hit. They had 15 Top 10 hits in the next four years. These included "It Must Be Love" (1981), "House Of Fun" (1982), "Our House" (1982) and "Wings Of A Dove" (1983).
** EVENTS **
1559 : Queen ELIZABETH I was crowned.
1752 : An Act for the "Change of Style" took effect in
England, stating that the New Year would begin on the 1st of January instead of the previously observed 25th of March.
1864 : American composer STEPHEN FOSTER, whose songs
included "SWANEE RIVER", died.
1921 : Windscreen wipers were introduced on cars for
the first time.
1926 : American lawman WYATT EARP, the hero of the
gunfight at the O.K CORRAL, died at the age of 81.
1939 : The worst bushfires in history hit Victoria, as
temperatues soared above 43 degrees. 71 people died, millions of hectares of forest were burnt, and several towns were lost in the firestorm.
1941 : Irish author JAMES JOYCE, whose book "ULYSSES"
caused outrage because of its sexual frankness, died after surgery in Zurich.
1957 : ELVIS PRESLEY recorded "ALL SHOOK UP" in
Hollywood.
1964 : The BEATLES' hit "I WANNA HOLD YOUR HAND" hit the
American pop charts at number 45.
1979 : American singer DONNY HATHAWAY fell to his death

from the 15th floor of the New York Essex House Hotel. Police were unable to determine whether it was intentional or an accident. Earlier on the same day he had been working with ROBERTA FLACK on a new LP.
1979 : Concorde began regular flights from Washington D.C
to Dallas.
1982 : An AIR FLORIDA jet crashed into the frozen Potomac
River near the White House, killing 78 people.
1982 : High Court judge SIR NINIAN STEPHEN was announced
as Australia's new Governor General. He was the third successive lawyer in the job and followed SIR ZELMAN COWEN who was leaving the post to become the Provost of Oriel College, Oxford.
1988 : New York doctors revealed that one in every 61
babies born last month in the city had AIDS.
